facts.fact: Presidential Decree 60/21 of 10 March 2021, the fee regulation of Angola's data protection agency (APD), lists an act of authorisation for international data transfer at a fee of Kz 350,450, so the APD's permission was a condition for sending personal data abroad; the document gives no date of effect other than its publication date, 2021-03-10.
facts.system: Regulamento das Taxas da Agência de Protecção de Dados (Tabela de Taxas da APD, item 1.7 Transferência internacional de dados)

note: Fee table for APD authorisations; the fee table, not guidance or a list of countries, so no fact on means or application.
Retained passages are an APD FAQ on fees, scope and the definition of personal data; none states a rule, means or application on sending data abroad.
Reports Angola's delegation saying its data protection law is in force; says nothing about sending data abroad.

slug: 2011-09-19 Angola Passes Personal Data Protection Law (Law 22-11)

facts.fact: Hunton reports that Angola's National Assembly passed Law 22/11 on 17 June 2011, under which the Data Protection Agency must approve international transfers to countries without adequate protection and controllers notify it of transfers to adequate countries; the note does not say when the law took effect.

note: Resolution approving the African Union convention; its text on national authorities authorising cross-border transfers is a treaty, not a national rule on sending data abroad.

facts.fact: Lei n.º 22/11, arts 33-34, makes transfer of personal data abroad to a country with adequate protection subject to notification to the APD, and to a country without it subject to APD authorisation on stated grounds such as the data subject's written consent; art. 67 puts the law in force on publication, 17 June 2011.
facts.system: Lei n.º 22/11 da Protecção de Dados Pessoais

note: No published list of countries, model terms or procedure appears; art. 34 leaves contract conditions for the APD to determine.

facts.fact: The APD fined Crescer Tech US$505,000 in 2026 for failing to notify and obtain authorisation for the international transfer of personal data to a cloud located abroad.

facts.fact: Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 that the APD fined Crescer Tech about USD 505,000 (c. 549 million kwanzas) for no notification or prior authorisation and an unauthorised international transfer to foreign cloud servers, and Fast Digital Center USD 112,000 (c. 110 million kwanzas) for inadequate security measures and no notification; deliberation dates are not given, so the publication date is used.
